title: Making AI-Enhanced Videos: Analyzing Generative AI Use Cases in YouTube Content Creation
venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA '25)
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative AI tools are being used in YouTube content creation, with a focus on understanding specific use cases across the video production workflow. The authors note that although tools like ChatGPT, MidJourney, and related systems are increasingly popular among creators, there was limited understanding of how these tools are actually applied throughout planning, production, editing, and uploading.

To address this, the study analyzed 274 YouTube how-to videos showing the use of GenAI in content creation. The researchers used thematic analysis to code 2,829 video clips and developed a conceptual framework of GenAI use cases across four phases: planning, production, editing, and uploading. The dataset was collected from YouTube videos posted between September 2023 and February 2024, filtered to English videos with captions and durations in a specified range, and then manually screened for relevance to GenAI-based video creation.

The findings show that creators use GenAI for tasks such as identifying video topics, generating scripts, refining prompts, creating images, avatars, voiceovers, and music, as well as editing tasks like lip-syncing, restyling, increasing resolution, clipping long videos, and translating speech. In the uploading phase, GenAI is used to generate subtitles and titles. The paper concludes that GenAI is already deeply embedded in creator workflows and argues for future tool designs that better support prompting, multimodal content creation, accessibility, and transparency around AI-generated media.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative thematic analysis of YouTube how-to videos, not an experiment or causal evaluation. It is peer-reviewed and methodologically systematic, but it primarily documents use patterns rather than testing outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests meaningful productivity support for content creators, but it does not estimate effect sizes on learner or creator outcomes. Its impact is therefore indirect and observational, with unclear magnitude for educational settings.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT and similar generative AI tools are used to segment transcripts, refine prompts, generate video scripts, suggest topics, titles, and subtitles, and support YouTube content-creation workflows.

finding.finding_summary: The paper finds that generative AI is widely used to streamline YouTube video production workflows across planning, production, editing, and uploading. In the 274-video sample, creators used GenAI for scripting (n=85), image/video generation (n=167), voiceover creation (n=93), and automatic subtitle generation (n=28), indicating substantial workflow support rather than a measured causal effect on performance.
finding.measure: Qualitative content analysis of GenAI use cases in YouTube how-to videos; frequency counts of observed use cases
